IGUI_TLG_Manual_Text:
1. START-UP

Build a Fermentation Vessel at a table or counter and place it. Choose Load mash and start fermenting: sugar or crops (corn, potatoes, sugar beets, pumpkins, watermelons, fruit), clean water (5 L for each kg of sugar) and yeast. It takes about 4 days when warm.

Place a Pot Still within two tiles of the finished vessel. Load wash from a nearby fermenter, Feed the firebox with wood, then Collect ethanol into a fuel can that is empty or holds only ethanol. A pot still takes 60 L of wash at a time, a Reflux Column Still 120 L.

Dry ethanol with quicklime in an Ethanol Drying Column and collect it about 12 hours later.

Keep the Yeast Starter Culture from a batch of 5 kg of sugar or more: it replaces bought yeast.

2. COMPATIBILITY

Stock gasoline engines run on up to 15 percent ethanol, struggle up to 25 percent and are damaged by more.

A converted (flex) engine runs on any blend of gasoline and ethanol, but starts poorly on near-pure ethanol in the cold. Convert a generator or a car from its menu: Workshop: convert this generator (or vehicle).

Pot still ethanol (about 80 percent) holds too much water for any engine until it is dried. Reflux ethanol (about 94 percent) runs flex engines as it is; dry it before blending it with gasoline, or the blend separates.

Stale, wet or dirty fuel starts harder and costs power.

3. TROUBLESHOOTING

Engine will not start on fresh-looking fuel: water, or the wrong fuel for that engine. Take a sample, drain the water or convert the engine.

Fermenter paused, too cold: it slows below 18 °C and stops below 8 °C, and three days stopped spoil the batch. Status shows the temperature at the machine; move it indoors or beside a lit fire.

Still paused, firebox out of fuel: Feed the firebox.

Wash is left: collect the still's ethanol, then load wash again.

Machine paused, picked up: place it on the ground.

Spoiled batch: Abort batch empties it.

Condition unknown: the fuel was never sampled. Look and smell, or take a sample with a kit.
